scenarios.name: single, moderate income, 3.51% bracket -- NE's 2026 Form 1040N is not yet published, so this uses the latest published (2025) primary figures per the task's 'or latest published' allowance
scenarios.source: As of this fixture's writing (August 2026), the Nebraska DOR has not published the TY2026 Form 1040N, tax calculation schedule, or standard deduction chart (only the TY2025 return and a TY2026 EMPLOYER WITHHOLDING circular exist, and the withholding circular's percentage-method rate structure -- 2.26/3.22/4.21/4.35/4.48/4.60% -- is a withholding approximation keyed to a $2,440/year 'withholding allowance' value, not the statutory Form 1040N bracket/deduction schedule, so it is not used here). This case uses the 2025 Nebraska Individual Income Tax Booklet (8-307-2025), page 13, Form 1040N Line 6 'Nebraska Standard Deduction Chart': single, 0 boxes checked on line 2a, standard deduction $8,600. The 2025 Nebraska Tax Calculation Schedule for Individual Income Tax (8-460-2025), Single Taxpayers table, second bracket: '4,030  24,120  $99.14 + 3.51% of the excess over $4,030'. Taxable income 30,000 - 8,600 = 21,400 falls in this bracket: tax = 99.14 + 0.0351*(21,400-4,030) = 99.14 + 609.687 = 708.827, rounds to 708.83. Nebraska Schedule III instructions, Line 7 / Form 1040N line 18: 'Nebraska Personal Exemption Credit for Residents Only... $171 times the number of exemptions'; one exemption (self) = $171. Net tax = 708.83 - 171 = 537.83. No age threshold or AGI phase-out gates NE's retirement-income treatment (pensionExemption/iraWithdrawalExemption both .none per the audit, socialSecurityExempt true separately), so this case and the next vary income rather than age.

knownDefect.summary: Not a retirement-exclusion defect (the audit's .none is correct); NE's engine stateDeduction ($12,000 single) is stale against the real 2025 published figure ($8,600), and the $171-per-exemption personal credit (Form 1040N line 18) is not modeled at all.

scenarios.name: single, high income with IRA withdrawal and Roth conversion, top 5.20% bracket
scenarios.source: Same 2025 Tax Calculation Schedule (8-460-2025), Single Taxpayers table, top bracket: '38,870  --  $1,543.28 + 5.20% of the excess over $38,870'. Standard deduction (same booklet, page 13, Line 6 chart) $8,600 single, 0 boxes. Taxable income 100,000 - 8,600 = 91,400 falls in this bracket: tax = 1,543.28 + 0.052*(91,400-38,870) = 1,543.28 + 2,731.56 = 4,274.84. Personal exemption credit (Form 1040N line 18, $171 * 1 exemption) = 171. Net tax = 4,274.84 - 171 = 4,103.84.

knownDefect.summary: Same mechanism as the low-income NE case: stale $12,000 standard deduction against the real $8,600, and the $171 personal exemption credit entirely unmodeled.

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses present, moderate combined income including Social Security, top 5.20% bracket
scenarios.source: This is the batch's MFJ 'both spouses present' case; NE has no age-gated retirement exclusion for either spouse to qualify for, so both are simply present. Nebraska excludes Social Security entirely from Nebraska AGI (2025 Form 1040N Schedule I Part B, line 31: 'Social security included in Federal AGI'; also LB 754's 2025 full SS exemption, cited in the app's own StateTaxData.swift comment for Nebraska), so state income before deduction is 160,000 - 30,000 = 130,000; standard deduction (2025 booklet page 13, MFJ 0 boxes) $17,200; taxable income = 130,000 - 17,200 = 112,800. 2025 Tax Calculation Schedule, Married Taxpayers Filing Jointly table: 112,800 exceeds both the second bracket's ceiling ($48,250) and the third bracket's ceiling ($77,730), so it falls in the fourth (top) bracket: '77,730  --  $3,086.10 + 5.20% of the excess over $77,730'. Tax = 3,086.10 + 0.052*(112,800-77,730) = 3,086.10 + 1,823.64 = 4,909.74. Personal exemption credit: two exemptions (self + spouse) * $171 = $342. Net tax = 4,909.74 - 342 = 4,567.74.

knownDefect.summary: Same standard-deduction and personal-exemption-credit gaps as the single NE cases, doubled for MFJ ($24,000 stale deduction vs the real $17,200, and $342 of unmodeled credit).

scenarios.name: MFJ, highest income in the batch, top 5.20% bracket
scenarios.source: Same 2025 Tax Calculation Schedule, Married Taxpayers Filing Jointly table, top bracket: '77,730  --  $3,086.10 + 5.20% of the excess over $77,730'. Standard deduction (page 13, MFJ 0 boxes) $17,200; taxable income 150,000 - 17,200 = 132,800. Tax = 3,086.10 + 0.052*(132,800-77,730) = 3,086.10 + 2,863.64 = 5,949.74. Personal exemption credit: two exemptions * $171 = $342. Net tax = 5,949.74 - 342 = 5,607.74.

knownDefect.summary: Same standard-deduction and personal-exemption-credit gaps as the other three NE cases.
